items.followUp: What happens to the DNA during the S-phase of the cell cycle?

rubric.why: Identifies the main event of S-phase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that DNA is copied or duplicated.

rubric.why: Explains why DNA replication is needed before division.
rubric.description: DNA replication prepares the cell to pass a complete set of genetic material to each daughter cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking DNA duplication to the later cell division or daughter cells receiving genetic material.

modelAnswer: During S-phase, DNA is replicated and the chromosomes are duplicated.
This ensures that each daughter cell can receive a complete set of genetic material during cell division.

items.followUp: What is synapsis? State when it occurs in meiosis.

rubric.why: Defines crossing over by identifying what exchanges segments.
rubric.description: Crossing over is the exchange of corresponding segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the exchange between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.

rubric.why: The diagram should show the exchanged segments between two chromatids.
rubric.description: Diagram shows a segment exchanged between two non-sister chromatids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a clear labelled diagram or equivalent before-and-after representation of segment exchange.

modelAnswer: Crossing over is the exchange of corresponding segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during prophase I of meiosis.
Diagram (before → after): Chromatid 1: A—B—C—D → A—B—c—d; Chromatid 2: a—b—c—d → a—b—C—D (segments exchanged between non-sister chromatids).

items.followUp: Define nondisjunction and state one possible result of it.

rubric.why: Describes the normal separation that occurs in disjunction.
rubric.description: In disjunction, homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids separate normally during cell division.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the chromosomes or chromatids separate normally.

rubric.why: Identifies the failure of separation that distinguishes nondisjunction.
rubric.description: In nondisjunction, homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids fail to separate properly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the chromosomes or chromatids fail to separate.

modelAnswer: In disjunction, homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids separate normally during cell division.
In nondisjunction, homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids fail to separate properly.

items.followUp: What structure forms the cell plate during cytokinesis in plant cells?

rubric.why: Identifies the structure and its role in forming the cell plate.
rubric.description: A phragmoplast is a structure made of microtubules that forms between the daughter nuclei during plant-cell cytokinesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the phragmoplast.

rubric.why: Explains the importance of the phragmoplast in plant-cell division.
rubric.description: It guides cell-plate formation, which develops into a new cell wall separating the daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the phragmoplast to cell-plate formation or separation of the daughter cells.

modelAnswer: A phragmoplast is a structure of microtubules that forms between the daughter nuclei during cytokinesis in a plant cell.
It guides the formation of the cell plate, which develops into a new cell wall separating the daughter cells.

items.followUp: Draw a labelled diagram showing the three phosphate groups in ATP.

rubric.why: Shows the adenine and ribose parts of ATP.
rubric.description: The diagram shows adenine attached to ribose (together called adenosine).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for showing or naming adenine and ribose as the adenosine portion.

rubric.why: Shows that ATP has three phosphate groups attached to adenosine.
rubric.description: The diagram shows three linked phosphate groups attached to ribose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a diagram or description that clearly shows all three phosphate groups attached to adenosine.

modelAnswer: Label adenine + ribose as adenosine, and the three linked phosphate groups as triphosphate (ATP).

items.followUp: Write the balanced chemical equation for photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Defines photosynthesis by identifying the raw materials and energy source.
rubric.description: Photosynthesis is the process in which green plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an accurate definition including the materials used and light energy.
Award 1 mark for the correct balanced equation.

modelAnswer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water.

items.followUp: What is the optimum pH of an enzyme? Give one suitable example.

rubric.why: Defines optimum temperature in terms of enzyme activity.
rubric.description: Optimum temperature is the temperature at which an enzyme works at its maximum rate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining it as the temperature of maximum enzyme activity or reaction rate.

rubric.why: Provides a suitable example of an optimum temperature.
rubric.description: Many human enzymes have an optimum temperature of about 37°C.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable example, such as human enzymes working optimally at about 37°C.

modelAnswer: Optimum temperature is the temperature at which an enzyme works at its maximum rate.
For example, many human enzymes have an optimum temperature of about 37°C.

items.followUp: Write two characteristics of enzymes other than those listed in your answer.

rubric.why: Recognises the catalytic role of enzymes.
rubric.description: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up biochemical reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes are biological catalysts or speed up reactions.

rubric.why: Checks for a second valid characteristic of enzymes.
rubric.description: A valid characteristic is that enzymes are specific, are not used up in reactions, or are affected by temperature or pH.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one valid characteristic distinct from the first.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up biochemical reactions.
Enzymes are specific: each enzyme acts on particular substrate(s).
